PART I

Item 1. Business

ExampleCo Inc. designs, manufactures and markets consumer electronics, software and related services worldwide. The Company sells its products through its retail stores, online stores and direct sales force, as well as through third-party cellular network carriers, wholesalers, retailers and resellers. The Company's fiscal year is the 52- or 53-week period that ends on the last Saturday of September.

Item 1A. Risk Factors

We depend on a limited number of suppliers for key components.

Substantially all of the Company's hardware products are manufactured by outsourcing partners that are located primarily in Asia. A significant concentration of this manufacturing is performed by a small number of outsourcing partners, often in single locations. If supply of a key single-sourced component were to be delayed or constrained, the Company's business and operating results could be materially adversely affected.

Cybersecurity incidents could disrupt our operations and harm our reputation.

The Company experiences malicious attacks and other attempts to gain unauthorized access to its systems on a regular basis. These attacks seek to compromise the confidentiality, integrity and availability of confidential information and could disrupt the availability of services. Losses or unauthorized access to or releases of confidential information could subject the Company to significant litigation, fines and reputational harm. During fiscal 2023 the Company observed a substantial increase in ransomware and extortion-based attacks targeting its supply chain partners, which could result in production interruptions.

Evolving regulation of artificial intelligence may impose new obligations on our products.

Governments in the United States, Europe and Asia are considering or have enacted legislation regulating the development and deployment of artificial intelligence features such as those integrated into the Company's devices and services. Compliance with divergent AI regulations could increase development costs, delay feature launches in certain jurisdictions and expose the Company to fines, litigation and reputational damage.

PART II

Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

Net sales for fiscal 2023 were $383.3 billion, a decrease of 3% compared to fiscal 2022, driven by lower sales of hardware products, partially offset by growth in services. Gross margin percentage increased to 44.1% primarily due to a favorable mix shift toward services. Operating expenses grew 4% year over year, reflecting continued investment in research and development. The Company generated operating cash flow of $110.5 billion during fiscal 2023 and returned capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk

The Company is exposed to interest rate risk on its investment portfolio and foreign exchange risk on international revenue and expenses. A hypothetical 100 basis point increase in interest rates would not have a material impact on the fair value of the Company's investment portfolio.

Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data

The consolidated financial statements of the Company, together with the report of the independent registered public accounting firm, are included herein. Net sales were $383,285 million and net income was $96,995 million for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2023. Total assets were $352,583 million at fiscal year end.

Item 9A. Controls and Procedures

Based on an evaluation under the supervision of management, the Company's principal executive officer and principal financial officer have concluded that the Company's disclosure controls and procedures were effective. Management did not identify any material weakness in internal control over financial reporting as of September 30, 2023.
